[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Security, RBAC, and TLS Configuration in Elasticsearch"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Securing an Elasticsearch cluster is a critical operational requirement. This tutorial covers enabling built-in security features, configuring Transport Layer Security (TLS) for encrypted communication, and implementing Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Enabling Elasticsearch Security"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, basic security features may not be automatically enabled depending on your distribution. You must explicitly set the configuration in the elasticsearch.yml file to activate security."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"xpack.security.enabled: true
xpack.security.transport.ssl.enabled: true
xpack.security.http.ssl.enabled: true"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Generating Certificates for TLS"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Elasticsearch requires certificates to encrypt traffic between nodes (transport layer) and between clients and the cluster (HTTP layer). Use the elasticsearch-certutil tool to generate a Certificate Authority (CA) and node certificates."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"./bin/elasticsearch-certutil ca
./bin/elasticsearch-certutil cert --ca elastic-stack-ca.p12"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Configuring TLS in elasticsearch.yml"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Place the generated certificate files into the config/certificates directory of your Elasticsearch installation. Then, update your elasticsearch.yml to reference these paths."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"xpack.security.transport.ssl.enabled: true
xpack.security.transport.ssl.verification_mode: certificate
xpack.security.transport.ssl.keystore.path: certificates/elastic-certificates.p12
xpack.security.transport.ssl.truststore.path: certificates/elastic-certificates.p12

xpack.security.http.ssl.enabled: true
xpack.security.http.ssl.keystore.path: certificates/elastic-certificates.p12
xpack.security.http.ssl.truststore.path: certificates/elastic-certificates.p12"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Setting Up Built-in Passwords"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once security is enabled, you must set passwords for the built-in system users. Run the interactive setup tool from your terminal."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"./bin/elasticsearch-setup-passwords interactive"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Implementing Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"RBAC allows you to assign specific privileges to users via roles. You can create custom roles using the Kibana interface or via the Elasticsearch REST API."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"POST /_security/role/log_writer
{
  "cluster": ["monitor"],
  "indices": [
    {
      "names": ["logs-*"],
      "privileges": ["write", "read", "create_index"]
    }
  ]
}"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 6: Assigning Roles to Users"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"After creating a role, you can map it to a specific user account. This ensures the user only has access to the indices and cluster actions explicitly granted to their assigned roles."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"PUT /_security/user/app_user
{
  "password" : "StrongPassword123!",
  "roles" : [ "log_writer" ],
  "full_name" : "Application User",
  "email" : "app_user@example.com"
}"},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always secure transport and HTTP layers with TLS to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Apply the principle of least privilege when configuring RBAC roles for users and applications."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regularly rotate your internal passwords and cryptographic certificates."}]
